name: Panama City
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Panama City: banking centre diligence, shipping and canal trade, corporate structures and asset research.
hero_lede: Panama City is the banking, legal and logistics centre of Panama, generating most of the country's output around the canal, its ports and an international banking centre. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for Panama City matters, working with Panamanian counsel and appropriately authorised local professionals.
intro: Panama City is the capital of Panama and the seat of its government, courts, regulators and most of its professional firms. Its economy is built on services: banking, commerce, logistics and tourism, with the city producing more than half of national GDP. The international banking centre grew from trade finance for canal traffic, and around 80 banks have operated in the city. The Pacific entrance of the Panama Canal, the port facilities at Balboa and Tocumen International Airport connect the city to world trade, while the Colón Free Zone on the Caribbean side, one of the largest free trade zones in the Americas, is closely tied to Panama City trading houses, law firms and banks.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Panama City because so many international structures are administered from it. Panamanian sociedades anónimas and private interest foundations are formed and maintained through resident agents and law firms in the city, and they appear in ownership chains for vessels, real estate, trading companies and investment holdings worldwide. Banks, ship registries and free zone traders generate trade finance, re-export and correspondent banking exposures. Clients need to identify who stands behind a Panamanian entity, trace assets held through local structures, verify counterparties in shipping and trade, and support litigation or arbitration seated in the city.

matters.title: Beneficial ownership of Panamanian entities
matters.text: Sociedades anónimas and private interest foundations formed in Panama City often sit in offshore ownership chains. We work from Public Registry filings, directors and resident agents, litigation and media records to identify likely controllers, recognising that shareholders and beneficiaries are generally not public.

matters.title: Shipping and vessel ownership research
matters.text: Panama's ship registry and the maritime law firms of Panama City support fleets owned worldwide. We trace registered owners, managers and related single-ship companies, maritime court records and casualty or detention history to support charterers, financiers, insurers and counsel pursuing vessel arrests or claims.

matters.title: Free zone and re-export trade diligence
matters.text: Trading houses linked to the Colón Free Zone and Panama City offices handle re-exports across Latin America. We test counterparties' ownership, trading history, litigation and adverse media for signs of trade-based money laundering, sanctions exposure or under-invoicing before clients extend credit or distribution rights.

matters.title: Banking and correspondent counterparty reviews
matters.text: Panama City's international banking centre serves regional and offshore clients. We support compliance teams and investors reviewing banks, payment intermediaries and their principals, using regulatory notices, corporate filings and court records to identify enforcement history, ownership changes and reputational concerns.

matters.title: Real estate and asset tracing
matters.text: Coastal towers and commercial property in Panama City are frequently held through corporations or foundations. We use Public Registry property entries by finca number, corporate filings and court records to connect assets to debtors or defendants, supporting recovery and enforcement planned with Panamanian counsel.

local_context.title: Courts and maritime jurisdiction
local_context.text: The Supreme Court of Justice and the main courts of the First Judicial Circuit sit in Panama City, where commercial and civil claims are heard by circuit courts. Panama also has specialised Maritime Courts for shipping disputes, vessel arrests and maritime liens, which give the city a significant role in international maritime litigation. Counsel decides the forum; our research is scoped to the evidence and procedures that court will apply.

local_context.title: Arbitration in Panama City
local_context.text: The Centro de Conciliación y Arbitraje de Panamá (CeCAP) marked its thirtieth anniversary in 2024 and administers domestic and international cases in the city. The Panama Maritime Law Association has also promoted a maritime conciliation, mediation and arbitration centre, Cecomap, to handle shipping disputes. Panamanian courts have been described by practitioners as pro-arbitration, and investigative support for arbitrations seated in the city is planned around the tribunal's evidence rules.

local_context.title: Public Registry and ownership data
local_context.text: The Public Registry, headquartered in Panama City, records corporations, foundations and real property, and its entries show directors, officers, resident agents and property encumbrances. Beneficial ownership information filed by resident agents under Law 129 of 2020 is held in a confidential single registry available to competent authorities, not to private researchers, so ownership work relies on public filings and corroborating sources.

local_context.title: Financial and non-financial supervisors
local_context.text: The Superintendency of Banks of Panama supervises the banking centre, and the Superintendency of the Securities Market oversees the Latinex exchange and brokers. Resident agents, lawyers and Colón Free Zone users fall under the Superintendency of Non-Financial Subjects created by Law 124 of 2020, with the Financial Analysis Unit receiving suspicious transaction reports. Published sanctions and resolutions from these bodies are useful lawful sources in counterparty reviews.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Panama City and handles Panama City matters from Nashville. We define the purpose first, whether a shipping claim, an arbitration with CeCAP, an asset recovery against a Panamanian foundation or counterparty screening for a bank or free zone trader, and agree scope with the client's counsel and, where needed, Panamanian counsel. Research draws on Public Registry entries, court and maritime court records, regulator resolutions, vessel data and media in Spanish and English. Because we have not confirmed a specific licensing regime for investigators in Panama, any local inquiries are carried out by appropriately authorised professionals engaged through counsel, without pretexting or access to restricted registries.

faqs.q: Can you find out who owns a Panamanian sociedad anónima?
faqs.a: Often partly. Public Registry entries show directors, officers, subscribers and the resident agent, but shareholders and beneficial owners are generally not public, and the beneficial ownership register under Law 129 of 2020 is confidential. We combine registry data with litigation, vessel, property and media records to build an evidence-based picture of likely control, with confidence levels stated.

faqs.q: Do you support maritime claims and vessel arrests in Panama?
faqs.a: We support counsel handling claims before Panama's Maritime Courts by researching registered owners, managers, related single-ship companies and fleet movements, and by identifying other assets of a debtor group. Arrests and filings are matters for Panamanian maritime lawyers; our role is to supply sourced information that helps them plan and act.

faqs.q: Is Panama City a suitable seat for arbitration support work?
faqs.a: Panama City hosts the Centro de Conciliación y Arbitraje de Panamá, active for about thirty years, and practitioners describe Panamanian courts as supportive of arbitration. We provide background research, witness profiles and asset information for arbitrations seated there, structured to the tribunal's procedural orders and confidentiality obligations.

faqs.q: How do you screen a Colón Free Zone trading company?
faqs.a: We review corporate filings, directors and resident agents, court and regulatory records, import and export patterns where public data allows, and Spanish and English media for sanctions, smuggling or money laundering allegations. We also map related companies in Panama City and elsewhere in Latin America that may share principals with the trading company.

faqs.q: Are private investigators licensed in Panama?
faqs.a: We have not confirmed a dedicated licensing statute for private investigators in Panama. Private security firms are supervised by the Ministry of Public Security, and whether investigative services fall within that regime should be confirmed with Panamanian counsel. TDSC does not hold any Panamanian authorisation and coordinates local work through counsel and suitably authorised professionals.
